Appendix No. III, 'Comparative vocabulary of the languages of some parts of Torres Strait' (pp. 274 ff; columns Erroob, Lewis's Murray Island, Massied, Cape York [1st and 2nd party], Port Lihou), with preface and 'rules observed in the spelling' pp. 274-277.
sources.note: No statement. The preface gives an orthographic convention for the whole comparative table: quantity (macron/breve) marks over vowels instead of accent marks, and rule 4 'The accent or quantity is marked by the long and the short [signs]' - i.e. any marks on Cape York items are wordlist-only data, not a rule for where stress falls. Jukes adds that nothing could be learned of grammatical structure. His phonetic remarks (clear enunciation, an aspirated d/dz sound, no f / soft g / x) describe the Erroob and Murray Island (Meriam) speakers; mainland Australians are characterised only as having 'm…
